notes: Founded by former IDE plugin engineers; product is an embeddable copilot for VS Code, JetBrains, and a lightweight web editor.
Usage pattern: heavy synchronous completions when devs hit ctrl-space and continuous streaming for inline suggestions; peak concurrency during 09:30-17:30 local (multi-region).
Primary ask: reserved capacity to eliminate noisy-neighbor P99 spikes during office hours and a configurable burst pool for release days.
Latency requirement: interactive completion latency <= 50ms median, P99 under load ideally < 120ms. Streaming handshake must start < 20ms to show suggestions quickly.
Need per-customer and per-workspace model pinning; some enterprise clients require a frozen model for compliance and reproducibility.
Fall back behavior: automatic fallback to quantized 8-bit variant with preserved API surface when primary model unavailable; prefer deterministic token output for tests.
Observability: request-level tracing tied to editor-session-id, per-route token cost, and retention of logs for 180 days for enterprise contracts.
Security: SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, KMS integration, SOC2/ISO27001 evidence required before purchase. EU customers require data residency by workspace.
Cost: aligns on committed monthly spend if Redwood can demonstrate <$0.04 per completion on average for their workload profile.
Quote from Head of Platform: 'We can't ship a bad completion experience on release day. Need predictable throughput at dev peak.'
POC outline: provision a dedicated pool (N small GPUs + 1 burst group) for 10 days; reproduce synthetic editor traffic (1.5k concurrent short completions) and run real-user beta in staging.
Observed during internal dry-run: kernel warm-up affects initial 30s of burst; suggested pre-warming strategy and prefix cache to reduce tail latencies.
